subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
description: This course introduces the structure, functioning, and interconnection of hardware components that constitute a computer system. It focuses on the organization and architecture that support efficient instruction execution and system performance.
objectives: Understand the basic structure and functional units of digital computers.
Explain instruction formats, addressing modes, and the principles of instruction execution.
Describe various types of memory systems and input/output organization.
Analyze processor performance through pipelining and parallelism.
Understand control unit design and arithmetic operations in computer architecture.
course_outcomes: Identify and explain the functional units of a computer and how they interact.
Illustrate the design and implementation of arithmetic and logic units.
Understand memory organization, cache mapping, and virtual memory concepts.
Analyze instruction cycle, addressing modes, and control flow.
Evaluate system performance using pipelining and input-output mechanisms.
